Intuitive Machines Inc (NASDAQ:LUNR) shares fell Wednesday as space stocks slid, with the move linked to weakness around SpaceX sentiment. Space Exploration Technologies Corp. (NASDAQ:SPCX), which is reportedly planning a $40 billion debt raise to buy Nvidia Corp. (NASDAQ:NVDA) chips, was down roughly 3.5% at last check.

The Financial Times reported that SpaceX is seeking about $10 billion in bank loans and $30 billion in investment-grade debt. Apollo Global Management is expected to lead the deal and sell the debt to a range of investors, with a 2027 close.

Apollo is one of six firms that teamed up with Nvidia in August on financing platforms meant to mobilize more than $500 billion for AI infrastructure. The other five are BlackRock, Blackstone, Brookfield Asset Management, Goldman Sachs and KKR.

LUNR is sensitive to SpaceX news because SpaceX launches its lunar missions, and investors often trade space stocks as a single theme. At publication, LUNR was down 7.10% at $14.00.
headline: Intuitive Machines Falls Wednesday as Space Stocks Track SpaceX Debt Report
summary: Intuitive Machines dropped about 7% to $14.00 as space stocks fell on sympathy with SpaceX's planned $40 billion debt raise for Nvidia chips.
